destinations.title: Thailand travel guide: destinations, seasons and entry preparation
destinations.description: Choose Thai cities and islands, compare monthly weather, and prepare your TDAC and passport-specific entry requirements before your trip.
destinations.intro: Imagine the days you would like to spend in Thailand: relaxing at a comfortable hotel, walking between temples and cafés, or taking a seaside holiday. Explore the cities and islands below and choose places that suit the way you want to travel.

bangkok.name: Bangkok
bangkok.intro: Rest at a hotel with a pool during the day, then enjoy riverside dining or rooftop night views in the evening. Bangkok suits a trip combining time at a five-star hotel with city sightseeing.

chiang-mai.name: Chiang Mai
chiang-mai.intro: Walk past temples and through Old City lanes, stopping at a café that catches your eye. Choose Chiang Mai for unhurried days with coffee and neighbourhood walks.

chiang-rai.name: Chiang Rai
chiang-rai.intro: See the distinctive colours and shapes of the White Temple and Blue Temple. Visit the buildings you have seen in photographs and explore northern Thailand’s mountains and temples.

pattaya.name: Pattaya
pattaya.intro: Walk along the beach or rest at your hotel during the day, then have dinner looking out to sea. Combine a seaside holiday with places to eat and explore in town.

hua-hin.name: Hua Hin
hua-hin.intro: Stay by the sea with your family, walk along the beach in the morning and visit markets in the evening. Choose Hua Hin for shared meals and rest without a packed sightseeing schedule.

phuket.name: Phuket
phuket.intro: Give sea-view resort days and Old Town outings separate space in your trip. Enjoy a beach holiday as well as walks and meals among streets of colourful buildings.

krabi.name: Krabi
krabi.intro: Walk along beaches beneath limestone cliffs rising beside the sea. Alternate restful days by the shore with boat outings to islands for different ways to enjoy the coast.

samui.name: Koh Samui
samui.intro: Enjoy a late breakfast at a seaside resort, walk along the beach and return for a rest. Take time over meals and relaxation with your partner or family.

phi-phi.name: Phi Phi Islands
phi-phi.intro: See cliffs rising from the sea and views between the islands. Explore by boat or look out from a viewpoint to experience the Thai island scenery you have seen in photographs.

phangan.name: Koh Phangan
phangan.intro: Consider Koh Phangan for beach relaxation and nights with music. Choose your beach and travel dates for either a lively atmosphere or a quieter break.

tao.name: Koh Tao
tao.intro: If you are curious about the underwater scenery as well as the beaches, consider Koh Tao. Learn to snorkel or dive, then finish the day relaxing beside the sea.

lanta.name: Koh Lanta
lanta.intro: Read at accommodation by the sea and walk along the beach as the sun sets. Choose Koh Lanta if you would rather stay longer on a beach you like than seek a new attraction every day.

samet.name: Koh Samet
samet.intro: Add a short seaside break to a Bangkok trip. Walk along white sand and eat by the sea, leaving time to rest after exploring the city.

destinations.entryIntro: Planning a trip to Thailand? Start with the entry rules for your passport and travel purpose, then complete the TDAC using your passport, tickets and accommodation booking. If you need a visa, choose the category and application process that match your plans.
destinations.seasonsIntro: Have you chosen your travel month? Compare the weather for temple and market walks in Bangkok or a beach break in Phuket or Koh Samui. Monthly temperatures and rainfall help you choose when to go and what to pack.

regions.name: Bangkok
regions.intro: For walks around Bangkok’s Grand Palace, temples and riverfront, plan a trip in **November–February**. Rainfall drops sharply from November after the wet months of September and October. December and January average about 27°C, making them less hot than April. Average daytime highs still exceed 32°C, so visit temples in the morning, walk beside the river around sunset, and leave time for meals and indoor breaks in between.

December and January have noticeably cooler mornings and nights, so pack a light layer. For mountain trips, use the forecast for your destination rather than the city’s observation figures when deciding what to wear.

entry.title: Entering Thailand: TDAC, passport and arrival guide
entry.description: Prepare your TDAC, check entry eligibility for your passport and travel purpose, and follow the airport arrival process from immigration to baggage claim.
entry.intro: Chosen your dates for Bangkok or Phuket? Check the entry conditions for your own passport and travel purpose, then complete your TDAC for your arrival date in Thailand. Keep your passport, ticket and accommodation booking beside you as you enter the details. This guide takes you from documents to prepare before departure through immigration and baggage collection after landing.

sections.title: Start with the rules for your passport
paragraphs: Visa exemption depends on **passport nationality, passport type and purpose of travel**. English-language guidance does not mean that every reader has the same eligibility. Use the official Thai e-Visa website to check your nationality and travel document, and read the instructions of the Thai embassy or consulate responsible for where you are applying. Check each traveller separately if family or friends hold different passports.

An advertised maximum stay is not automatically granted to every arrival. After immigration, check the **actual admitted-until date** recorded in your passport and leave within that permission. If you will work, study or stay for a longer purpose, prepare the relevant visa rather than relying on tourist entry conditions.

sections.title: What to have ready before your flight
paragraphs: Keep your passport, ticket and accommodation booking together. Enter your **name exactly as it appears in your passport** and use the booking’s English accommodation name and address for the TDAC. Read the Thai arrival date and flight number from your ticket, rather than copying the date you leave your departure country.

Have your return or onward ticket and accommodation details ready. If asked where you will stay or when you will leave, explain your booked itinerary. Check the financial evidence required for your passport and entry category in the responsible Thai mission’s official instructions. Funds required as evidence of your trip are separate from TDAC submission, which is free.

sections.title: Complete the TDAC within three days, including arrival day
paragraphs: The TDAC is the online arrival declaration replacing the paper arrival card. **Non-Thai nationals entering Thailand** by air, land or sea must complete it before immigration, subject to the official exemptions. Children need their own traveller details too.

Submit **within the three-day window that includes your arrival date**. Prepare your passport, ticket, English accommodation address and email, and use the local arrival date in Thailand. Download the completed document to your phone so you can open it at the airport even with an unreliable connection.
Completing an arrival declaration does not issue a visa. **TDAC and visa preparation are separate**. If your purpose requires a visa, prepare both the visa and the TDAC.

sections.title: After you land at the airport
paragraphs: Follow **Immigration / Passport Control** signs to the immigration area. Keep your passport, TDAC confirmation and any required visa easy to reach. Answer questions about your travel purpose and accommodation using your actual plans.

After immigration, read the permitted-stay expiry recorded in your passport. Continue to **Baggage Claim**, collect your bags and pass through customs to the arrivals hall. Use the declaration procedure if you have goods to declare. Routes differ between airports such as Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang, so read the guide for your arrival airport as well.

sections.title: Transit without entering Thailand
paragraphs: You do not need a TDAC if you **transit without passing immigration**. If you enter Thailand to leave the airport or collect bags and check in again, you need a TDAC.

If you booked separate tickets, ask the airline before departure whether your bags will be checked through and whether you must pass Thai immigration. An itinerary labelled “transit” can still require entry into Thailand.

faq.q: Do I need both a TDAC and a visa?
faq.a: Travellers entering under a valid visa exemption still need a TDAC unless an official TDAC exemption applies. The TDAC is an arrival declaration; a visa is a separate requirement based on your passport and travel purpose. A work or study trip cannot be prepared simply by completing the TDAC.

faq.q: How long can I stay without a visa?
faq.a: The applicable permission depends on your passport, passport type and purpose. Check your eligibility through the official Thai e-Visa website and responsible Thai mission. After arrival, use the actual permission recorded in your passport when planning your departure.

faq.q: Which date do I enter for a late-night arrival?
faq.a: Use the local arrival date in Thailand shown on your ticket. If you depart one day and land in Thailand the next, enter the next day’s date. Check the arrival date and flight number together.

entry.title: How to complete Thailand’s TDAC on your phone
entry.description: Follow the TDAC mobile form: passport and flight details, accommodation, health declaration, submission, offline document storage and corrections.
entry.intro: Keep your passport, ticket and accommodation booking beside you and work through the TDAC one screen at a time. The steps below explain names, the local arrival date in Thailand, flight numbers and accommodation details. After submitting, save the completed document on your phone so you can open it at the airport.

sections.title: Use the official website and the right submission window
paragraphs: Check that the address bar says **tdac.immigration.go.th**. This is the Immigration Bureau’s official website and **TDAC submission is free**. It is separate from the Thai e-Visa website.

Submit **within three days, including your arrival date in Thailand**. You need a new submission for every entry; a form from a previous trip cannot be reused. Have your passport, incoming flight number, local Thai arrival date, English accommodation address and an email address ready.

sections.title: Language settings and English entries
paragraphs: You can read the form in English or use the website’s language options or your browser’s page translation. The location of language and translation controls varies by device and browser.

**Enter the information in English**, even when reading translated instructions. Copy names and passport numbers exactly from the passport, and the accommodation address from the English booking confirmation. The screenshots below show the English mobile form so that you can find each button and field.

sections.title: Choose Arrival Card on the opening screen
paragraphs: To make a new submission, press **Arrival Card**. The neighbouring **Update Arrival Card** button is for changing a form you have already submitted. Start with Arrival Card for a first submission.

The opening screen also mentions 90-day reporting and work permission. This does not mean the TDAC lasts 90 days or authorises you to work in Thailand. Use Arrival Card for this trip’s arrival declaration.

sections.title: Personal Information: enter your passport details
paragraphs: Put your surname in **Family Name** and given name in **First Name**. Do not invent a Middle Name if your passport has none. Place each name in the corresponding field and copy your passport number into Passport No.

Nationality/Citizenship asks for your nationality; Date of Birth, Occupation and Gender ask for the corresponding personal details. Country/Territory of Residence is where you currently live, and City/State of Residence is your city or region. If you live outside your passport country, give the actual answer to each question rather than matching the two countries automatically.

Visa No. is the number of an issued visa. **Do not invent a visa number for visa-exempt entry.** Follow the required-field stars and distinguish optional fields. Enter the country calling code and phone number separately, then press Continue.

Retrieve with Passport is unavailable in the preserved screenshot. If you cannot use the passport MRZ reading feature described by the official guide, enter the details manually. If you do scan the passport, compare the retrieved names and number with the passport yourself.

sections.title: Arrival Information: use the journey arriving in Thailand
paragraphs: Trip Information has separate sections for **arrival in Thailand and departure from Thailand**. Start with Arrival Information and your incoming ticket. Use the local arrival date in Thailand and the flight arriving there, rather than simply copying your departure date.

For a holiday arriving on a scheduled passenger flight, select **HOLIDAY**, **AIR** and **COMMERCIAL FLIGHT**. These answers describe a holiday by air. Choose answers that match your actual trip if you are coming for business or study, or entering by land or sea.

Type the English country name or three-letter code, then **choose the result from the list**. The preserved Korean example uses KOR : REPUBLIC OF KOREA; that is an example, not the answer for every traveller. Confirm that the country you actually selected appears in the field.

fields: Date of Arrival
Enter the local Thai arrival date on your ticket in YYYY/MM/DD format. If the flight lands the day after departure, use that next day. You can also use the calendar.
Country/Territory where you Boarded
Select the country or territory where you boarded the flight arriving in Thailand. If you connected abroad, use where you boarded that final inbound flight.
Purpose of Travel
Use HOLIDAY for a holiday. Select MEETING, BUSINESS or EDUCATION only when it matches your actual purpose. OTHERS (PLEASE SPECIFY) requires the relevant explanation in English.
Mode of Travel
Choose AIR for a flight, LAND for a land crossing or SEA for arrival by boat. The transport options below change accordingly.
Mode of Transport
Choose COMMERCIAL FLIGHT for a regular passenger flight. Select PRIVATE/CARGO AIRLINE or OTHERS only if applicable.
Flight No./Vehicle No.

For air travel, enter the airline code and flight number of the flight arriving in Thailand. This is not the booking reference or seat number. Land and sea travellers should enter their actual transport details.

sections.title: Departure Information: use your journey out of Thailand
paragraphs: Below arrival details is **Departure Information**. Its date and flight number refer to **leaving Thailand**, not leaving your home country. With a return ticket, use the local departure date and flight number from Thailand.

Departure fields in the preserved screen have no mandatory star. Do not invent a date or flight if plans are not fixed. An optional form field does not remove the separate need to be ready to explain your return or onward plans at immigration.
Use **Clear** to reset an incorrectly selected departure travel mode. Read the headings so you do not confuse arrival AIR with departure AIR.

sections.title: Accommodation Information: copy your booked address
paragraphs: Open your accommodation booking and find the **English address in Thailand**. This section is not asking for your home address. Copy the hotel name, administrative area and address from the booking or the hotel’s official information.

Required fields can vary by accommodation type. In the preserved screen, choosing **HOTEL removes mandatory stars from District and Sub-District**. Follow the stars on your own form instead of applying that behaviour to every accommodation type.

Select the larger area first: Province, then District, Area, then Sub-District, Sub-Area. This enables the dependent lists. Choose the names matching the accommodation address, even if others look similar. For a Bangkok stay, the Province can be BANGKOK.

**I am a transit passenger, I don’t stay in Thailand** describes transit without a stay. Do not select it simply because you have not booked a hotel. It may be disabled depending on other answers. If you enter Thailand for a holiday and stay there, provide your actual accommodation details.

sections.title: Health Declaration: countries visited in the previous two weeks
paragraphs: List the **countries or territories where you stayed during the two weeks before arrival**. Include your actual recent stays. This is not the field for Thai cities you will visit later.

Type an English country name or code and choose the relevant search result. Passport nationality, residence, boarding country and recent stays are different questions. Do not copy the same country into every field unless it is correct.

The screen includes Ministry of Public Health vaccination information. The official guide explains that **additional health questions can appear** depending on recent countries, boarding country, nationality and flight. Answer the questions and provide evidence actually requested for your circumstances. The preserved screenshot is a basic example using Korea; it does not show every traveller’s possible questions.

Press **Preview** to review. Previous returns to the earlier step and Add Other Travelers adds another traveller. Use each person’s actual passport and travel history rather than copying one person’s country history for everyone.

Additional health information or evidence
Read the displayed applicability and questions, then answer using your own health and travel details. Do not copy answers from another traveller’s example.

sections.title: Preview: review the details and enter your email
paragraphs: Read your name, passport number, nationality and birth date again, together with **arrival date, boarding country, incoming flight and accommodation address**. Use **Edit** to correct mistakes. EXAMPLE in the preserved screenshot is demonstration text; no actual arrival declaration was submitted.

Enter an email address you can access in the **email field at the bottom**. It is not a name field. Check the spelling on both sides of @. Access to that inbox on your phone makes the completed document easier to find.
Read the **Terms and conditions**, tick acceptance yourself if you agree, then press **Submit**. The button is disabled without the required agreement. Viewing Preview alone does not submit the form.
If an error appears or no completed document is provided, do not assume submission succeeded. Look for the actual completion notice and TDAC document before saving them.

sections.title: After submission: download and save your TDAC
paragraphs: A successful submission provides **confirmation and the TDAC download**. The official video shows both. The preserved image is a **completion example from that official video**, captured in a mobile browser. The video contains an older desktop screen, so its layout can differ from the current mobile application.

Download the document and check that the name, passport details and arrival date match your trip. Keep the declaration number, QR code and confirmation details, and find the emailed copy too. Do not use the video’s example number or QR code for your own entry.
**Save the actual file so it opens offline**. Keeping only an email link is less useful if the airport connection is unreliable. You may also carry a printed copy.

Keep the confirmation available to show at entry and during your stay. **A completed TDAC is not a visa or permission to enter.** Visa exemption or visa eligibility and immigration inspection are separate.

sections.title: Correcting a submitted TDAC
paragraphs: Choose **Update Arrival Card** on the opening screen. The preserved search screen asks for the TDAC number, birth date, arrival date and nationality. Use your document and passport to complete the fields, then press **Search**.

The official FAQ says that **full passport name, passport number, nationality and date of birth cannot be updated**. If one of these is wrong, submit a new form with the correct details. For editable information such as accommodation, update and resubmit before entering Thailand, then save the new document.
The image shows the search for an existing submission. If you have never submitted, return to Arrival Card to make a new form instead of looking here for a TDAC number.

faq.q: Is TDAC submission free?
faq.a: Yes. Submission through the Immigration Bureau’s official website has no fee. Check that the address bar says tdac.immigration.go.th.

faq.q: Can I read instructions in another language?
faq.a: Yes. Use the website’s language options or browser translation, but enter the details in English. Copy passport information from the passport and the accommodation address from the English booking.

faq.q: Do children and visa-exempt travellers need a TDAC?
faq.a: Yes. Non-Thai travellers, including infants and children and those using visa exemption, need their own traveller details. Transit without passing Thai immigration is exempt.

faq.q: Does the TDAC issue a visa?
faq.a: No. The arrival declaration and visa are separate. Meet the visa-exemption conditions for your passport, or obtain the visa required for your purpose.

faq.q: Can I correct a misspelled name?
faq.a: Submit a new form with the correct name. Full name, passport number, nationality and birth date cannot be updated according to the official FAQ. Correct editable details through Update Arrival Card before entry, then resubmit and save the document.

faq.q: Is the flight number my booking reference?
faq.a: No. Enter the airline code and number of the flight arriving in Thailand in Flight No./Vehicle No., not the booking reference or seat number.

faq.q: Is the departure date the date I arrive home?
faq.a: No. Date of Departure is the local date you leave Thailand. Read the Thai departure details on your outbound ticket.

faq.q: Are District and Sub-District required for HOTEL?
faq.a: In the preserved screen, their required stars disappear after HOTEL is selected. Requirements vary by accommodation type, so follow the stars shown on your own form.

faq.q: Does the health declaration ask for my future Thai destinations?
faq.a: No. It asks for countries and territories where you actually stayed during the two weeks before arrival.

faq.q: Is submission complete when Preview opens?
faq.a: No. Preview is the review screen. After checking your email and the terms, submit and look for the success notice and completed TDAC document.

entry.title: Thailand visa types: tourism, work, study and longer stays
entry.description: Understand visa exemption, TDAC and Thai visa categories, then find the official application requirements for your passport, purpose and location.
entry.intro: A holiday, a job and a course of study require different preparation. Check whether your passport and holiday plans meet visa-exemption conditions before applying. Tourism permission cannot stand in for permission to work or study. Decide what you will do and how long you intend to stay, then choose the official category matching that purpose.

sections.title: Visa exemption, TDAC and visas have different roles
paragraphs: **Visa exemption** allows eligible travellers to enter without obtaining a visa in advance under the applicable conditions. **TDAC** is an online arrival declaration. A **visa** is applied for according to a purpose such as tourism, study or work. Completing TDAC does not issue a visa.

Check exemption eligibility for your passport on the official Thai e-Visa website and with the responsible Thai mission. Do not apply one family member’s nationality rules to everyone travelling. Reading this page in English does not establish nationality or eligibility.

sections.title: Choose a category matching your actual purpose
paragraphs: Decide what you will do in Thailand, then read the corresponding category below. The official e-Visa site separates purposes such as tourism, work and study. Similar category names do not mean identical eligibility or document requirements. Read the detailed requirements for your actual activity.

sections.title: Use Thai e-Visa and the responsible mission
paragraphs: Create an account at **thaievisa.go.th**, fill in the application and upload the requested documents. Complete any fee process and submit. Monitor the application status and email for requests for additional material. Once approved, save the visa confirmation sent to you.

Select your actual nationality, travel document and current location. Application jurisdiction depends on where you are applying; do not assume your nationality alone decides which embassy handles it. Read the instructions from the mission identified for your location before submission.

sections.title: Visa validity is different from permission to stay
paragraphs: Visa validity is the period during which the visa can be used. Permission to stay is the time granted after entering Thailand. A tourist visa’s use-by period and the duration of one admitted visit are different.

Approval does not mean you can remain until the last day of the visa’s validity. After immigration, check the **actual admitted-until date in your passport** and plan departure around it. An extension requires a separate application and decision; applying alone does not extend your stay.

faq.q: Does every tourist need a tourist visa?
faq.a: No. If your passport and trip meet the applicable visa-exemption conditions, you may not need a tourist visa. Work, study and longer stays need their own eligibility checks. Use the official lookup for your passport and purpose.

faq.q: Is DTV the same as a tourist visa?
faq.a: No. They are separate categories. DTV covers eligible Workcation or Thai soft-power activities; tourist visas cover tourism. Check the qualifications and documents for the activity you intend to undertake.

faq.q: Where do I apply for a Thai visa?
faq.a: Start at the official Thai e-Visa website using your real nationality, passport type and current location. Follow the identified Thai mission’s submission instructions and jurisdiction rules.

entry.title: Thailand tourist visa: entries, documents and e-Visa application
entry.description: Check whether you need a Thai tourist visa, understand validity versus permission to stay, and prepare the documents and online steps required by your mission.
entry.intro: Before applying for a tourist visa, check whether your passport and travel plans qualify for visa exemption. If you need a visa, decide whether your trip involves one entry or multiple entries. Use the official Thai e-Visa website and the Thai mission responsible for your application location to check documents, fees and the submission process.

sections.title: Single entry and multiple entries
paragraphs: Single-entry and multiple-entry visas differ in the number of permitted entries and the period during which you can use the visa. Read the validity and admitted-stay terms displayed for the category and mission handling your application. **Visa validity is not the length of one stay**.

If you need more time after arrival, check the applicable extension procedure with Thai immigration. **An extension application requires approval**. Do not plan your departure on the assumption that it will be granted; first read the permission recorded in your passport.
fields: Single-entry tourist visa
For one entry during the visa’s stated validity; check the applicable stay conditions.
Multiple-entry tourist visa
For eligible repeated entries during the stated validity; each stay has its own permission.
Extension
Separate application to Thai immigration; approval is required.

sections.title: Prepare documents for your passport and application location
paragraphs: Use the document list shown by **Thai e-Visa and the responsible mission**. Prepare a readable passport copy, photograph, itinerary and accommodation evidence as requested. Check the passport-validity and photograph-age requirements for that application rather than copying another country’s checklist.

Your location and residence status can affect supporting documents and jurisdiction. If applying outside your passport country, read the mission’s requirements for proof of lawful stay or residence. Korean residence cards and K-ETA evidence belong to applications in Korea and are not a worldwide checklist.

Financial evidence, required balances, statement periods and document issue dates can differ by category and mission. Use the stated requirements for your application. **Visa application bank evidence and cash evidence at immigration are different preparations**.

Use the flight itinerary and accommodation documents requested by the mission. If a host invitation is accepted, read whether host identification and address evidence must accompany it. An invitation alone may not provide all the requested evidence.

Read the actual document requests in the application and respond to any additional requests after submission. Uploading documents does not mean approval: the mission can seek more material or reject an application that does not meet its requirements.

sections.title: From online application to saving the approval
paragraphs: At **thaievisa.go.th**, create an account and enter your nationality, current location, passport type and tourist purpose. If passport details are read automatically, compare surname, given name and any middle name with the passport yourself.

Upload documents, complete the applicable fee process and press **Submit**. Fees and exemptions depend on the actual nationality and application; Korean fee exemptions are not universal. Check the selected passport type and the mission’s payment and refund conditions before submitting.

Follow the application status and email for further document requests. Once approved, download and save the e-Visa confirmation. Processing estimates are not guaranteed issue dates and additional checks can take longer. Apply with enough time before travel rather than relying on another mission’s processing estimate.

sections.title: A tourist visa does not replace TDAC
paragraphs: Even after receiving a tourist visa, **complete the TDAC separately** unless an official exemption applies. Submit through the official website within the three-day window including arrival day and save the resulting document on your phone.

At the airport, keep your passport and visa confirmation available. After immigration, read the actual permission-to-stay expiry in your passport. Plan departure around that permission, rather than the visa’s validity date.

faq.q: Do I need a tourist visa?
faq.a: Check visa-exemption eligibility for your passport, travel purpose and intended stay first. If the trip requires a tourist visa, apply for the category matching those conditions.

faq.q: Does multiple-entry validity mean I can stay for that entire period?
faq.a: No. The validity period tells you when the visa can be used; it is separate from the permission granted for each entry. After immigration, use the actual admitted-until date in your passport.

faq.q: What is the tourist visa fee?
faq.a: Check the amount and any exemption for your actual nationality and application on the official e-Visa site and responsible mission’s instructions. A fee exemption described for Korean nationals is not a worldwide rule. Follow any required payment-completion step.

faq.q: Can I travel as soon as I submit the application?
faq.a: Submission is not approval. Monitor status and email, respond to requests, and obtain the approval document. A published processing estimate does not guarantee an issue date.
